answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems are funnel-mechanics problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing it is the single lever that can move both. Two independent inherited records converge here (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on signup simplification), which is stronger evidential support than any single-source candidate. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the memory I intend to act on and I need to know what 'improved completion and time-to-value' actually measured — completion rate lift is easy to manufacture by removing steps without any gain in real adoption or revenue. I am verifying memory_73 second precisely because promotional pricing is the emotionally obvious answer to a competitor price attack and its consolidated summary reads over-strong ('strong acquisition and revenue lift', 'held across both billing plans'). Consolidated summaries tend to lose the caveats: I want to know the observation window, whether the 'revenue lift' was discounted revenue that never renewed, and whether retention was measured at all. Racing a competitor to the bottom on price is the most plausible way to hit short-term numbers while destroying sustainable long-term qualified revenue, which is the stated objective, so that is the claim most worth spending budget to falsify. I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44 because neither addresses the current funnel decline. Explicit downstream risk: memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows. Those interact badly — fewer signup fields means less firmographic data for routing, so a naive simplification could quietly divert enterprise-shaped prospects into self-serve and degrade pipeline quality even while activation metrics improve. So the experiment must be scoped to self-serve/SMB traffic only, must preserve whatever fields drive sales routing, and must be judged on downstream qualified revenue and retention rather than completion rate alone. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence is suggestive but the current quarter-over-quarter declines mean conditions have shifted since day 52, so the prior may be stale and needs re-confirmation at a scale where a wrong answer is cheap. Also note memory_91 (activation messaging) remains a reasonable fallback if verification undercuts memory_86; I am holding it rather than discarding it.
